ITF.title: Coral Triangle and the Indonesian Throughflow

dimensions.name: resolution
dimensions.description: the grid's range of cell sizes

dimensions.name: cell_size_ratio
dimensions.description: the largest cell size over the smallest

dimensions.name: product
dimensions.description: the ocean forcing product, such as glorys

dimensions.name: atmosphere
dimensions.description: the compset's DATM option, such as jra or nyf

dimensions.name: ice
dimensions.description: the compset's ice component: cice, dice or sice

properties.title: Turn off GM parametrization at high resolution
properties.message: Below 8 km, eddies are partly resolved, so GM thickness diffusion is usually turned off.

properties.title: The time step is set by the smallest cells
properties.message: Cell sizes in this grid differ by a factor of 2 or more, and the time step must suit the smallest cells everywhere. A grid with more even cells can run with a longer step: an area-conserving projection, or at high latitudes a polar one.
properties.instruction: Build the grid with mom6_forge's Grid.from_projection, using an equal-area projection, EPSG:3995 in the Arctic or EPSG:3031 in the Antarctic.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: You’ll have to set your time step based on the smallest grid cells in your domain
And if you’re working at higher latitudes, a polar projection would probably make more sense.

properties.title: The domain's edge crosses the Gulf Stream
properties.message: Open boundaries work best where strong currents cross them at right angles; where the Gulf Stream enters at a steep angle it reflects and causes artifacts.
properties.instruction: Move the edge, or rotate the grid (mom6_forge's Grid.from_center with angle_deg) so the current crosses it squarely.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: Open boundary conditions are more stable when energetic currents cross them perpendicularly.
Rotating your domain so that the main current crosses the boundary perpendicularly helps a lot.

properties.title: The domain's edge crosses the North Brazil Retroflection
properties.message: Strong currents are fine at a boundary; chaotic flow, with eddies in every direction, is not. An edge across the North Brazil Retroflection invites trouble.
properties.instruction: Take the whole structure into the domain, or move the edge well away from it.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: What’s problematic is chaotic flow—eddies in every direction.
If the current system includes something like a retroflection, that feature really needs to be included within the domain—placing a boundary right at a retroflection usually leads to trouble.

properties.title: Benguela: resolution helps, but biases persist
properties.message: Models keep a warm SST bias here even at high resolution. Local causes include coarse coastal winds that weaken the coastal jet and the upwelling; remote causes include tropical Atlantic SST biases that reach the region through the boundaries. The front between the Angola and Benguela currents, near 16°S, is tied to the bathymetry.
properties.instruction: Get the bathymetry and coastline right, then check the mean state: the currents, the position of the front and the cold SST of the upwelling. Tune the winds and the boundary inflow before mixing or viscosity.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: the Benguela still lags behind other upwelling systems in terms of model fidelity

properties.title: Force tides: tidal mixing dominates here
properties.message: This region is a maze of shallow basins and narrow straits where tidal mixing dominates, amplified by resonance in the passages. Models without tides make up for it by raising local mixing; with tides, the model mixes where it really happens.
properties.instruction: Give configure_forcings the TPXO files and these constituents, and check tidal phase and amplitude against the region's tide gauges.

changes.rationale: Tides here are semidiurnal, diurnal or mixed, so force both kinds

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: the region consists of many small, shallow, and interconnected basins with narrow straits, where intense tidal mixing plays a dominant role.

properties.title: Measure transport through the Indonesian Throughflow straits
properties.message: The Throughflow branches across several passages, and observations give the transport through each. Matching them is the main test of a model here.
properties.instruction: Compute transport through Makassar Strait, Lombok Strait, Ombai Strait and Timor Passage, and compare each with observed estimates such as the INSTANT moorings'. Agree the targets before tuning, and stop when the magnitudes match.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: One critical evaluation metric is the transport through the main ITF channels.

properties.title: Expect to edit the bathymetry of the Throughflow straits
properties.message: Realistic transport through each strait took 20 or more rounds of bathymetry edits; tuning viscosity was not enough. Interpolated, smoothed bathymetry often lowers sills or closes channels where a cell centre falls on land.
properties.instruction: Smooth for stability first, then restore sills toward their observed depths and open channels the land mask closed. If a strait still carries too much or too little, widen or narrow it, even if that departs a little from the observed bathymetry.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: The model required multiple iterations—potentially 20 or more—to arrive at a configuration that gave realistic transports.

properties.title: Lombok Strait spans only a few cells
properties.message: Lombok Strait is thousands of metres deep on either side of a sill about 200 m deep. Even at 5 km it spans only a few cells, and its steep slopes cause spurious diapycnal mixing unless smoothed.
properties.instruction: Count the cells across the strait, set its sill depth to observed estimates after smoothing, and compare its transport with observations.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: Even at a 5-km resolution, the strait might only span a few grid cells.

properties.title: Torres Strait is too coarse to leave open
properties.message: Torres Strait is very shallow, with near-zero mean transport. At coarse resolution one cell is too wide or too deep and lets far too much through, so many models close it.
properties.instruction: Close Torres Strait in the bathymetry, or check that its mean transport stays near zero.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: that strait might be represented by a single grid cell that’s too wide or too deep—leading to exaggerated transport.

properties.title: Keep Torres Strait open
properties.message: At this resolution the model can resolve the tidal reversals that dominate the strait's flow, while its mean transport stays near zero.
properties.instruction: Check that the strait is open in the bathymetry and that its mean transport is near zero.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: in higher-resolution configurations, it can be left open, and the model can then resolve tidal reversals

properties.title: Consider active sea ice (CICE)
properties.message: Part of this domain is poleward of 60 degrees, where sea ice forms in winter.

properties.title: Finer resolution pays off in the Arctic
properties.message: Global models struggle at high latitudes, where resolution is coarse and data sparse. A regional domain at about 1/10 of a degree can improve the simulation markedly.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: moving to a higher-resolution domain—on the order of 1/10°—can significantly improve simulation quality.

properties.title: For Antarctic overflows, topography is the main gain
properties.message: Higher resolution brings better dynamics and better topography. For dense-water overflows the topography matters most, because it sets their pathways; for SST or heat transport the dynamics matter more.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: if you work on Antarctic overflows,  the improved topography is the bigger gain because it's essential for capturing the pathways of dense water.

properties.title: Coral Triangle: consider rotating the grid to follow the flow
properties.message: A Coral Triangle configuration rotated by about 20 degrees lined its boundaries up with the main flows, and was about 30% smaller than a latitude-longitude box.
properties.instruction: Try a rotated grid (mom6_forge's Grid.from_center with angle_deg) so the main currents cross the open boundaries at right angles.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: rotated the grid by about 20 degrees to better match the orientation of the key flows. That also made the model about 30% smaller

properties.title: Evaluate coral heat stress the way satellites do
properties.message: Degree Heating Weeks come from satellite SST. Process the model's SST the same way before comparing. A high-resolution model can show local warming, as in upwelling zones, that satellite products miss.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: SST was important, especially for assessing coral stress using metrics like Degree Heating Weeks.

properties.title: Coarse winds weaken the Benguela upwelling
properties.message: This atmospheric forcing is coarse next to the coastal winds that drive the upwelling. Smoothed winds weaken the coastal jet and the upwelling, which warms the SST.
properties.instruction: If the upwelling matters to your study, consider finer winds, and compare the upwelling's SST with observations.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: insufficient resolution in the coastal wind forcing, which can weaken coastal jets and reduce upwelling.

properties.title: Where to put the edges of a Benguela domain
properties.message: Include the Benguela upwelling and part of the Angola coast. Extend west to at least 0°E, past the Cape of Good Hope, to take in the Agulhas retroflection. Stop short of the tropical Atlantic, where the flow turns zonal and would cross the northern boundary at a steep angle; the expert suggested a northern edge around 7°S.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: the domain might extend slightly west of the Cape of Good Hope to capture the Agulhas retroflection and reach north to just below the Angola–Benguela Front—perhaps around 7°S.

properties.title: Keep the Strait of Gibraltar open
properties.message: Gibraltar is under 50 km wide, about half a cell at 1 degree, but it is the Mediterranean's only exchange with the Atlantic. Closed, the Mediterranean grows far too salty.
properties.instruction: Edit the land mask and bathymetry to keep a channel open, and check the exchange and the salinity of the Mediterranean outflow.

references.title: Expert interview 1: Coral Triangle & Benguela Upwelling

evidence.quote: you cannot close it because it is the only exchange between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic.
